Subject: Private deploy questions — EU/APAC routing, key locality, and failover

Hi Ben,

Thanks for the demo yesterday. Our security team wants a concise plan for a private deployment (VPC/on-prem connector) covering two items before we proceed to purchase:

- Data residency guarantees across EU and APAC sites (what parts of logs/metadata may transit regions).
- Failover behavior: how an APAC failure impacts EU workloads and whether traffic ever transits through a third region.

Specific asks from our infra team: egress IP ranges to whitelist, BGP/peering expectation (static routes vs BGP), DNS TTLs for failover, and KMS/HSM locality for customer-managed keys. We also need evidence for audit (SOC2 artifacts + architecture diagram).

Can you send a short technical runbook and a network diagram we can hand to our cloud team? We are aiming for a pilot in mid-Jan.

Thanks,
Aisha Rahman
Head of Ops, GlobalMed Solutions

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Ops Team <ops@globalmed.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-24T16:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Private deploy questions — EU/APAC routing, key locality, and failover

Aisha, Ben — putting the technical guardrails here. I kept this actionable so your cloud team can use it as a checklist. We attached a network diagram (network-diagram-eu-apac-v2.png) and a draft failover checklist (runbook-failover-checklist.pdf).

Summary of recommended architecture (private deployment mode):
- Topology: customer VPCs in EU and APAC with a Redwood Private runtime deployed as dedicated nodes inside each VPC (air-gapped/private control plane). We offer two operational modes:
  1) Active/Passive (recommended for strict residency): EU active, APAC warm standby. Data (user payload, logs) written only to the active region’s storage; backups replicated to standby using encrypted snapshots. Minimizes cross-border writes.
  2) Active/Active (lower latency for global clients): state replicated across regions via encrypted replication (see notes below). This requires explicit legal sign-off for replication of derived telemetry.

Residency & logs:
- Application payload: pinned to customer storage in the active region.
- Audit logs & control-plane telemetry: by default routed to local logging endpoints (customer SIEM). We can optionally forward aggregated metrics to a central Redwood analytics plane; however, for sovereign deployments we set that to OFF by default.
- Metadata that may transit (e.g., health checks, heartbeat pings) are minimal and can be restricted to control-plane only within the selected regions.

KMS/HSM and key locality:
- Customer-managed keys: supported. Keys reside in your KMS/HSM in the region you choose (we do not escrow keys). We perform envelope encryption at the node level, with no plaintext persistence outside the node. For cross-region failover, keys must be available in the target region (recommended: replicate keys to a secondary KMS per your organization policy).

Networking & failover mechanics:
- Peering: we support IPsec site-to-site tunnels or cloud-managed VPC peering. BGP is supported for dynamic route failover (preferred) but static routes work for simpler setups.
- Egress IPs: we will provide a stable ASN/CIDR set to whitelist. For private deploys we minimize third-region egress; failover traffic stays between EU and APAC unless you request global proxying.
- DNS: low TTLs (30s–60s) recommended for rapid failover; we also support health-check-driven weighted DNS failover if you prefer no client-side retry.
- Ports: 443 outbound for control plane, 10250/10255 (K8s node agents) if you allow in VPC, and 514/UDP or 6514/TCP for syslog to customer SIEM. Exact ports in diagram.

State synchronization & caches:
- Model weights: stored locally per region; versions pinned explicitly.
- KV/prefix caches: warm-standby uses asynchronous replication — acceptable for most LLM inference workloads. If you require synchronous replication (zero-loss), that is only possible with Active/Active and will impact latency/cost.
- Session continuity: short-lived sessions may be lost on failover. We provide a session replay mechanism that replays recent KV fragments for sessions within a configurable window (default 5 minutes).

RTO/RPO expectations (baseline):
- Active/Passive: RPO = snapshots (default 15m), RTO = 5–15 minutes for routing + node spinup depending on warm standby size.
- Active/Active: RPO ~ near-zero depending on replication pipeline; RTO minimal but requires infra and legal approvals.

Operational runbook (high level):
1) Pre-cutover: agree CIDR list, create peering/IPsec, exchange BGP session params, pre-stage images in standby region, validate KMS access.
2) Dry-run: perform a simulated failover during a low-traffic window — fail traffic to standby, run smoke tests.
3) Production cutover (if active/passive): 10–30 minute maintenance window: update DNS weights, BGP withdraw + advertise, promote standby storage, rotate KMS if required.
4) Post-cutover: confirm telemetry, run a query sweep on pinned data to confirm locality, exchange signed confirmation.

Security & evidence for audit:
- We will provide a residency evidence bundle (residency-evidence-pack.zip) containing: SOC2 artifacts (redacted), network diagrams, KMS architecture notes, and a signed log-delivery confirmation.

Testing & constraints:
- We recommend a two-week pilot in EU with APAC warm-standby pre-staged; this minimizes customer risk and gives time to validate network policies.

Open items (need your decisions):
- Preferred operational mode: Active/Passive (default) or Active/Active?
- KMS key replication policy (replicate keys to APAC? yes/no)
- DNS provider constraints (can you support TTL=30s?)

I’ll join the cloud sync call to walk through the diagram.

— Karthik
Head of Infrastructure, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Aisha — following up with the materials Karthik outlined. Attached are the network diagram and the residency evidence bundle. A couple of pragmatic notes:

- Default recommendation: Active/Passive with warm standby in APAC. This gives strong residency guarantees while keeping failover time short.
- If you require keys to remain exclusively in EU at all times, we will operate in EU-only for the pilot; failover would require a signed exception and an agreed failover window that may include manual approvals.

Proposed next steps and timeline:
- Confirm mode (Active/Passive) and TTL constraints by 2026-12-09.
- Schedule a 45-minute tech sync for 2026-12-07 (I’ll share a calendar invite once you confirm availability).
- We’ll run the dry-run failover the week of 2027-01-09, with a production pilot targeted for 2027-01-16.

If you’re good with the above I’ll also send a formal security questionnaire to your cyber team (allows us to lock down any telemetry concerns).

Thanks — Ben
